Downgrade of status is not permitted under any circumstances once granted. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 is correct — CPSEs can be upgraded through tiers (Miniratna to Navratna to Maharatna) upon meeting prescribed criteria. Statement 2 is incorrect — status can, in principle, be reviewed and downgraded if a CPSE fails to sustain the required performance.

advanced.q: With reference to strategic sectors identified under the 2021 public sector enterprise policy, which of the following is generally included among the specified strategic sectors?
advanced.e: The 2021 PSE policy identifies a small set of strategic sectors — including atomic energy, space and defence, transport and telecommunications, power/petroleum/coal and other minerals, and banking/insurance/financial services — warranting a continued, though minimal, public sector presence.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Disinvestment receipts and asset monetisation receipts are both accounted for as capital receipts in the Union Budget, though through different heads. 2. Asset monetisation under NMP directly increases the government's outstanding public debt. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 is correct — both are treated as capital receipts, though recorded under distinct heads (disinvestment vs. non-debt capital receipts from asset monetisation). Statement 2 is incorrect — monetisation of existing assets generates receipts without creating a new debt/borrowing obligation, unlike loans.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. A CPSE's shares being partly held by the public (post-listing) automatically triggers a change in its Maharatna/Navratna status. 2. Maharatna/Navratna status is linked to financial performance criteria and is independent of whether the CPSE's shares are listed or fully government-owned. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 is incorrect — listing alone does not automatically alter Maharatna/Navratna status. Statement 2 is correct — the classification is based on financial performance criteria (net worth, turnover, profit, global presence, etc.), applicable regardless of whether the CPSE is listed, as long as government retains requisite ownership.

title: Economic Survey, Budget Documents & Key Indices
desc: Economic Survey, Budget documents, global rankings and indices

basic.q: The Economic Survey of India is typically presented in Parliament:
o: A month after the Union Budget
One day before the Union Budget
On the same day as the Union Budget, after it
Three months before the Union Budget
basic.e: The Economic Survey is conventionally presented in Parliament one day before the Union Budget, providing a review of the economy and outlook.

basic.q: Who is primarily responsible for preparing the Economic Survey of India?
o: The Chief Economic Adviser (CEA) and the Department of Economic Affairs
The Reserve Bank of India Governor
basic.e: The Economic Survey is prepared under the guidance of the Chief Economic Adviser (CEA), in the Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance.

basic.q: Is the Economic Survey a legally binding policy document that the government must implement?
o: Yes, it is a legally binding statute
No, it is essentially an analytical/advisory document reflecting the government's assessment and views, not binding legislation
Yes, it has the same legal status as the Finance Bill
It becomes law once tabled in Parliament
basic.e: The Economic Survey is an analytical and advisory document reviewing economic performance and suggesting policy directions; it is not a legally binding statute.

basic.q: Which of the following is a money bill presented along with the Union Budget that gives effect to the government's taxation proposals?
basic.e: The Finance Bill contains the government's taxation proposals for the year and is presented along with the Budget.

basic.q: Which Bill is passed to give the government legal authority to withdraw funds from the Consolidated Fund of India to meet expenditure for various services and purposes?
basic.e: The Appropriation Bill authorises the government to withdraw funds from the Consolidated Fund of India for the expenditure detailed in the Budget.

basic.q: Which Budget document sets out the assessment of prospects for growth in the economy, along with the fiscal indicators as mandated under the FRBM Act?
basic.e: The Macroeconomic Framework Statement, mandated under the FRBM Act, presents an assessment of the economy's growth prospects and underlying macro parameters.

basic.q: The Ease of Doing Business rankings (erstwhile 'Doing Business' report) were published annually by which international organisation, until discontinuation of the report?
basic.e: The 'Doing Business' report, which produced the Ease of Doing Business rankings, was published by the World Bank Group until it was discontinued in 2021 following data irregularity concerns.

basic.q: The Global Hunger Index (GHI) is jointly published by which organisations?
basic.e: The Global Hunger Index is published jointly by Concern Worldwide (Ireland) and Welthungerhilfe (Germany), two non-governmental organisations.

basic.q: The Global Competitiveness Index/Report was historically published by which organisation?
basic.e: The Global Competitiveness Report, including the Global Competitiveness Index, was published by the World Economic Forum.

basic.q: Which of the following best describes the primary content of Volume I of the Economic Survey?
o: Only detailed state-wise sectoral statistical tables
Analytical chapters discussing the state of the economy, key themes and policy issues
Only the government's revenue and expenditure statement
A list of new taxation proposals
basic.e: Volume I of the Economic Survey contains thematic, analytical chapters on the state of the economy and important policy issues, while Volume II typically presents a sector-wise review with data.

basic.q: The Union Budget in India is presented under which constitutional provision, referring to the 'Annual Financial Statement'?
basic.e: Article 112 of the Constitution mandates the presentation of the 'Annual Financial Statement' (commonly called the Union Budget) before Parliament.

basic.q: Which of the following statements about the date of presentation of the Union Budget is correct?
o: It has always been presented on the last day of February since Independence
It was advanced to 1 February from 2017 onwards, from the earlier practice of presenting it on the last working day of February
It is presented on 1 April every year
It is presented on 1 January every year
basic.e: Since 2017, the Union Budget has been presented on 1 February, advanced from the earlier tradition of presenting it on the last working day of February.

basic.q: Which document, part of the Budget, explains the tax proposals and their expected revenue implications in narrative form, often released alongside the Finance Bill?
o: Memorandum Explaining the Provisions of the Finance Bill
basic.e: The Memorandum Explaining the Provisions of the Finance Bill narrates the rationale and implications of the tax proposals contained in the Finance Bill.

basic.q: 'Demands for Grants' presented with the Union Budget represent:
o: The estimated expenditure requirements of various ministries/departments, requiring Lok Sabha's approval before Appropriation Bill is passed
A list of foreign grants received by India
Loans given by India to other countries
Grants given to state governments only under the Finance Commission
basic.e: Demands for Grants present ministry/department-wise estimated expenditure requiring the Lok Sabha's voting/approval, which subsequently forms the basis for the Appropriation Bill.

basic.q: Who among the following holds/held the position of Chief Economic Adviser, a role central to preparing the Economic Survey?
o: A position within the Reserve Bank of India
An officer/economist appointed by the Government of India in the Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance
An elected member of the Lok Sabha
A judge of the Supreme Court
basic.e: The Chief Economic Adviser is a senior economist appointed by the Government of India, functioning within the Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance, to advise on economic policy and helm the Economic Survey's preparation.

basic.q: Which of the following is NOT typically considered one of the key Budget documents mandated to be presented under the FRBM Act along with the Annual Financial Statement?
o: Medium-Term Fiscal Policy cum Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement
basic.e: The Global Hunger Index Report is an independent international publication, not a Budget document; the other three are part of India's budget documentation.

basic.q: The 'Vote on Account' is a mechanism used by Parliament to:
o: Permanently replace the Union Budget for the entire financial year
Grant the government advance authorisation to meet essential expenditure for a limited period pending full Budget approval
Approve new tax rates for the coming five years
basic.e: A Vote on Account allows the government to draw funds from the Consolidated Fund to meet essential expenditure for a short period (e.g., in an election year), pending passage of the full Budget.

basic.q: Which of the following organisations publishes the annual 'World Competitiveness Ranking' (a related but distinct index from the WEF's competitiveness index)?
basic.e: The World Competitiveness Ranking is published by the IMD World Competitiveness Center, distinct from the (discontinued) WEF Global Competitiveness Report.

intermediate.q: Which of the following statements about the Economic Survey's timing and status is correct?
o: The Economic Survey is presented after the Budget to explain already-announced measures
The Economic Survey is presented a day before the Budget and is not a binding document but reflects the government's own assessment of the economy and suggested reforms
The Economic Survey and the Union Budget are the same document
The Economic Survey is prepared by the Reserve Bank of India
intermediate.e: The Economic Survey is tabled a day before the Budget; being an analytical document prepared by the CEA's team, it is not binding, though it often previews the thinking behind subsequent budget proposals.

intermediate.q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Finance Bill from the Appropriation Bill?
o: The Finance Bill deals with government expenditure while the Appropriation Bill deals with taxation
The Finance Bill gives effect to taxation proposals, while the Appropriation Bill authorises withdrawal of funds from the Consolidated Fund of India for sanctioned expenditure
Both bills deal exclusively with taxation and have no difference
The Appropriation Bill is passed before the Budget is presented
intermediate.e: The Finance Bill implements taxation changes, whereas the Appropriation Bill legally authorises the government to draw money from the Consolidated Fund for the expenditure voted by Parliament.

intermediate.q: Which of the following statements about the discontinuation of the World Bank's 'Doing Business' report is correct?
o: It was discontinued because all countries achieved the highest possible ranking
It was discontinued in 2021 following concerns about data irregularities and undue pressure in rankings of some countries, including China
It continues to be published annually without any changes
It was merged permanently with the Global Hunger Index
intermediate.e: The World Bank discontinued the 'Doing Business' report in 2021 after an investigation revealed data irregularities and alleged undue pressure on rankings for some countries.

intermediate.q: Which of the following statements about the Global Hunger Index (GHI) is correct?
o: It is compiled using indicators such as undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting, and child mortality
It measures only the GDP growth rate of countries
It is published by the Government of India
intermediate.e: GHI scores are calculated using four indicators: undernourishment, child wasting, child stunting, and child mortality, to assess hunger levels across countries, largely developing/emerging economies.

intermediate.q: Which of the following statements about the Macroeconomic Framework Statement is correct?
o: It is an optional Budget document with no legal backing
It is mandated under the FRBM Act and gives an assessment of the growth prospects of the economy along with fiscal indicators like GDP growth, fiscal deficit, and external sector balance
It replaces the Finance Bill entirely
It only contains data about foreign exchange reserves
intermediate.e: The Macroeconomic Framework Statement is a legally mandated document (under the FRBM Act) providing an overview of macroeconomic prospects, including growth, fiscal balance and external sector indicators.

intermediate.q: Which of the following statements correctly describes the structure of the Economic Survey?
o: It usually comprises two volumes: Volume I with analytical/thematic chapters and Volume II with a review of current developments and sector-wise performance with statistical appendix
It comprises only one chapter on taxation
It is published only once every five years
It is identical in content to the Union Budget speech
intermediate.e: The Economic Survey is generally structured into Volume I (thematic/analytical chapters) and Volume II (review of the year, sector performance, statistical appendix).

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Economic Survey is presented to Parliament before the Union Budget every year without exception. 2. The Economic Survey has, on occasion, been presented as a single document without separate volumes. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct — the Survey is conventionally presented before the Budget, and in some years it has been presented as a single consolidated volume rather than in two separate volumes.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Global Competitiveness Index was discontinued by the World Economic Forum in its traditional ranking format after 2019, with WEF later shifting focus to other frameworks. 2. The IMD's World Competitiveness Ranking continues to be published annually and is a separate index from the WEF's report. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct — the WEF discontinued its Global Competitiveness Report in its earlier ranking form after 2019/2020, while the IMD World Competitiveness Ranking remains a distinct, continuing publication.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Finance Bill, being a Money Bill, can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha. 2. The Rajya Sabha has no role whatsoever in relation to a Money Bill and cannot even offer recommendations. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct — a Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha. Statement 2 is incorrect — the Rajya Sabha can discuss and make recommendations on a Money Bill within 14 days, though the Lok Sabha may accept or reject them.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Chief Economic Adviser's office is responsible only for the Economic Survey and has no other advisory function. 2. The Chief Economic Adviser typically advises the Finance Minister and the government on macroeconomic policy issues throughout the year, beyond the Survey itself. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is incorrect — the CEA's role extends beyond just the Survey. Statement 2 is correct — the CEA advises the government on macroeconomic issues on an ongoing basis, not just during Survey preparation.

intermediate.q: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the Global Hunger Index and India's participation in it?
o: India's own government agencies compile and submit the underlying survey data exclusively for GHI

The GHI relies on data largely drawn from international sources such as the FAO and UNICEF/WHO for its four component indicators, and India's official position has periodically contested the index's methodology
GHI covers only economic growth statistics and not nutrition indicators
India has never featured in the Global Hunger Index
intermediate.e: GHI indicators are constructed using data primarily from bodies like FAO, UNICEF and WHO; the Indian government has at various points questioned the index's methodology, particularly regarding the undernourishment estimation approach.

intermediate.q: Which of the following statements about the 'Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement' (part of the Medium-Term Fiscal Policy cum Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement) is correct?
o: It outlines the government's strategic fiscal policy priorities, including tax and expenditure policies, for the ensuing year, in line with FRBM Act requirements
It has no connection with the FRBM Act
It replaces the need for a Union Budget entirely
It is prepared exclusively by the Reserve Bank of India
intermediate.e: The Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement, mandated by the FRBM Act, outlines the government's strategic priorities on taxation, expenditure and other fiscal policy matters for the year.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The 'Output Budget' presented by ministries reviews physical and financial performance of schemes/programmes against targets. 2. The Output Budget is a mandatory constitutional document like the Appropriation Bill. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 correctly describes the Output Budget, a performance-review document for schemes. Statement 2 is incorrect — it is an administrative/performance document, not a constitutionally mandated bill like the Appropriation Bill.

intermediate.q: Which of the following best explains why the Ease of Doing Business rankings mattered for India's policy discourse before their discontinuation?
o: They had no bearing on India's reform agenda
They were used as one benchmark to track progress on regulatory/business-environment reforms, influencing India's ranking-linked reform initiatives across states and sectors
They exclusively measured India's defence readiness
They replaced the need for GDP growth statistics
intermediate.e: The Ease of Doing Business rankings served as a widely cited benchmark tracking regulatory reform progress, motivating India's efforts (including state-level 'Business Reform Action Plans') to improve its ranking before the report's discontinuation.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Economic Survey chapters are typically authored/coordinated by the Economic Division of the Department of Economic Affairs under the Chief Economic Adviser. 2. The Economic Survey must be approved by both Houses of Parliament through a formal vote before the Budget can be presented. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect — the Survey is tabled in Parliament for information/discussion but does not require a formal approval vote as a precondition for the Budget.

intermediate.q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'Revenue Budget' from 'Capital Budget' as components of the Annual Financial Statement?
o: Revenue Budget deals with receipts/expenditure not affecting government's assets/liabilities, while Capital Budget covers receipts/expenditure that affect assets and liabilities (e.g., loans, asset creation)
Revenue Budget covers only capital expenditure
Capital Budget deals only with tax revenue
There is no such distinction in Indian Budget documents
intermediate.e: The Revenue Budget covers current receipts (tax/non-tax revenue) and expenditure not resulting in asset creation, while the Capital Budget covers receipts/expenditure affecting the government's assets and liabilities, such as loans and capital asset creation.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The term 'Pink Book' informally refers to the Union Budget's Expenditure Budget or Demands for Grants documents in some contexts. 2. The Union Budget documents are placed in the public domain after being formally presented in Parliament. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 2 is correct — Budget documents are released publicly once presented in Parliament. Statement 1 is not an established standard usage in the Indian budgeting context and is incorrect as commonly referenced.

intermediate.q: Which of the following statements about the 'Budget at a Glance' document is correct?
o: It provides a summary snapshot of key Budget aggregates such as total receipts, expenditure, deficit figures and allocations to major sectors/schemes
It is a legally binding bill requiring parliamentary passage separate from the Appropriation Bill
It contains only state-wise foreign direct investment data
It is prepared by the Election Commission of India
intermediate.e: 'Budget at a Glance' is a concise summary document presenting key aggregates of receipts, expenditure, deficits and major allocations, aiding quick reference, distinct from the detailed Budget bills.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Economic Survey is presented under a specific constitutional mandate similar to the Union Budget under Article 112. 2. Unlike the Union Budget, presentation of the Economic Survey is a convention/practice, not a specific constitutional requirement. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 is incorrect — there is no specific constitutional article mandating the Economic Survey's presentation (unlike Article 112 for the Budget). Statement 2 is correct — the Survey's presentation is a long-standing convention/practice, not a constitutional obligation.

advanced.q: With reference to the FRBM Act, 2003 and its associated Budget documents, consider the following statements: 1. The Act mandates presentation of the Macroeconomic Framework Statement, Medium-Term Fiscal Policy cum Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement along with the Annual Financial Statement. 2. The FRBM Act originally mandated a Medium-Term Expenditure Framework Statement as well, detailing expenditure projections for the following three years. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct — besides the Macroeconomic Framework and Fiscal Policy Strategy statements, the FRBM Act framework also envisaged a Medium-Term Expenditure Framework Statement outlining three-year rolling expenditure projections.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Economic Survey's forecasts and analysis often set the intellectual tone and inform subsequent budget proposals, but the Finance Ministry is not obligated to adopt Survey recommendations. 2. Different editions of the Economic Survey have, at times, carried special thematic focus chapters or 'think pieces' distinct from the routine sector reviews. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct — the Survey often shapes the discourse ahead of the Budget without binding the government to its suggestions, and various editions have carried special analytical/thematic chapters on topics of contemporary policy interest.

advanced.q: Which of the following statements correctly explains why India's methodology-based critique of the Global Hunger Index centres on the 'proportion of undernourished population' indicator?
o: India argues this indicator is based on a small sample opinion poll called the 'Gallup World Poll' capturing perceived food insecurity rather than actual calorie intake, and hence may not accurately reflect ground realities
India argues the indicator overstates hunger because it uses satellite imagery of crop yields only
India has never contested any methodology of the GHI
The indicator in question measures GDP per capita rather than hunger
advanced.e: India's stated objection has centred on GHI's use of a proxy/opinion-based measure of food insecurity (drawing on surveys like the Gallup World Poll for one component) rather than direct nutritional/calorie-intake data, arguing this may not accurately capture actual undernourishment.

advanced.q: With respect to the Union Budget's classification of expenditure, consider the following statements: 1. Under the current budgeting framework, the distinction between 'Plan' and 'Non-Plan' expenditure has been discontinued and replaced by the 'Revenue' and 'Capital' expenditure classification as the primary framework. 2. This change was implemented from the 2017-18 Budget onwards, alongside the merger of the Railway Budget with the General Budget. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct — the Plan/Non-Plan classification was discontinued in favour of Revenue/Capital expenditure classification, and this reform coincided with the merger of the Railway Budget into the General Budget from 2017-18.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The 'Fiscal Deficit' figure presented in the Budget represents the excess of total expenditure over total receipts excluding borrowings. 2. The Macroeconomic Framework Statement is required to comment on the fiscal deficit and its financing pattern as part of its mandated disclosures. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct — fiscal deficit is total expenditure minus total receipts excluding borrowings, and the Macroeconomic Framework Statement is mandated to assess fiscal indicators including the deficit and its financing.

advanced.q: Which of the following is the most accurate statement about the relationship between the Economic Survey and Union Budget in terms of sequencing and institutional authorship?
o: Both documents are prepared entirely by the same team with identical content and are legally identical in status

The Economic Survey, authored under the CEA in the Department of Economic Affairs, is presented a day earlier as an economic review/outlook document, while the Union Budget, presented by the Finance Minister, contains the government's actual fiscal proposals and is a constitutionally mandated Annual Financial Statement requiring parliamentary approval
The Union Budget is prepared before the Economic Survey by several years
The Economic Survey requires presidential assent to come into force, unlike the Budget
advanced.e: The Economic Survey (CEA-authored review/outlook, non-binding) precedes the Union Budget (Finance Minister's constitutionally mandated Annual Financial Statement under Article 112, requiring parliamentary approval) by roughly a day, reflecting their distinct institutional roles.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The World Bank's 'Doing Business' rankings measured regulatory ease across parameters such as starting a business, getting credit, paying taxes and enforcing contracts. 2. Following the report's discontinuation, the World Bank has worked on developing a successor assessment framework for business environment evaluation. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct — 'Doing Business' assessed multiple regulatory parameters like starting a business, credit access, taxation, and contract enforcement, and after its discontinuation in 2021, the World Bank pursued a successor initiative for business environment assessment.

advanced.q: With reference to the 'Charter of Budget' documents in India, consider the following statements: 1. The 'Expenditure Budget' provides ministry/department-wise details of budget provisions, distinguishing between revenue and capital expenditure. 2. The 'Receipt Budget' details estimates of revenue and capital receipts, along with explanatory notes on tax and non-tax revenue. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct — the Expenditure Budget gives ministry-wise revenue/capital expenditure details, while the Receipt Budget details revenue and capital receipt estimates with explanatory notes.

advanced.q: Which of the following statements best explains why the Global Hunger Index and India's official hunger/nutrition estimates (e.g., from NFHS) sometimes diverge in emphasis?
o: NFHS and GHI use identical methodology and always produce matching results

GHI is a composite cross-country comparative index using specific proxy indicators standardized globally, whereas national surveys like NFHS use India-specific, more granular anthropometric and health survey methodology, leading to potential differences in emphasis and figures
NFHS does not measure child nutrition at all
GHI is prepared using only Indian government data submissions
advanced.e: GHI is a standardised, cross-country comparative index relying on globally harmonised proxy indicators, while NFHS (National Family Health Survey) uses India-specific, more granular survey methodology — a key reason for occasional divergence in reported figures/emphasis.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The 'Statement of Fiscal Policy' and 'Statement of Fiscal Risks' are examples of transparency-oriented disclosures introduced under FRBM-related amendments in some years to flag contingent liabilities. 2. Contingent liabilities from government guarantees are a recognised fiscal risk factor that such statements aim to disclose. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct — enhanced fiscal transparency disclosures, including recognition of contingent liabilities (e.g., from government guarantees), have been incorporated into India's fiscal reporting framework over time to flag potential fiscal risks.

advanced.q: With respect to institutional authorship, which of the following statements is correct?
o: The Chief Economic Adviser is appointed by and reports to the Reserve Bank of India Governor

The Chief Economic Adviser is appointed by the Government of India and functions under the Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance, distinct from the RBI's own research/monetary policy functions
The Chief Economic Adviser chairs the Monetary Policy Committee
The Chief Economic Adviser is elected by Parliament
advanced.e: The Chief Economic Adviser is a government appointee under the Ministry of Finance's Department of Economic Affairs, distinct from the RBI, which has its own research wing and Monetary Policy Committee (chaired by the RBI Governor).

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Union Budget's 'Annual Financial Statement' must show separately the expenditure 'charged' upon the Consolidated Fund of India and expenditure 'to be voted' by Parliament. 2. Charged expenditure includes items such as salaries/allowances of the President, and debt charges for which government is liable, and this expenditure is discussed but not put to a vote in Parliament. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct — the Annual Financial Statement distinguishes 'charged' expenditure (e.g., President's emoluments, debt servicing), which is discussed but not voted upon, from expenditure requiring a parliamentary vote.

advanced.q: Which of the following best captures a key limitation commonly associated with global indices like the Ease of Doing Business or Global Competitiveness Index, as noted in policy debates?
o: These indices are always perfectly objective with zero scope for perception-based bias

Some of these indices rely partly on expert/perception-based surveys, cover a limited set of cities/respondents, and may not fully capture the diversity/complexity of a large, federal economy like India
These indices are calculated using only satellite data with no survey component
There is universal consensus that no index has ever had any methodological criticism
advanced.e: A recurring critique is that indices combining perception-based surveys with limited city/respondent coverage may inadequately capture the full diversity of a large, federal economy like India, where conditions vary significantly across states.

advanced.q: With reference to Budget presentation practices, consider the following statements: 1. Prior to 2017, the Railway Budget was presented separately from the General Budget, a practice followed since the colonial era. 2. The merger of the Railway Budget with the General Budget was intended to reflect the railways' revenue and expenditure within the overall national fiscal picture. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct — the separate Railway Budget tradition (dating back to the 1920s, based on the Acworth Committee recommendation) was merged into the General Budget from 2017-18, integrating railway finances into the overall fiscal picture.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Economic Survey's macroeconomic projections (e.g., GDP growth estimates) are prepared independently of the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation's official data releases and never draw upon them. 2. The Survey typically draws upon and analyses official data from bodies such as the National Statistical Office, RBI, and other government agencies. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 is incorrect — the Survey's analysis draws heavily on official statistics. Statement 2 is correct — it synthesises data from sources like the National Statistical Office, RBI, and various ministries to build its assessment.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements regarding key global indices relevant to the Indian economy: 1. The Global Hunger Index score is expressed on a 100-point scale where a lower score indicates a better (less severe) hunger situation. 2. Countries are grouped into severity categories (e.g., low, moderate, serious, alarming, extremely alarming) based on their GHI score. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct — GHI scores range on a 100-point severity scale (lower is better), and countries are classified into severity categories such as low, moderate, serious, alarming and extremely alarming.

advanced.q: Which of the following is the most accurate description of the distinction between the erstwhile World Bank 'Doing Business' rankings and the WEF's 'Global Competitiveness' rankings?
o: Both measured exactly the same set of parameters with no conceptual difference

'Doing Business' focused narrowly on regulatory ease for domestic firms across specific processes (e.g., registering property, enforcing contracts), while the Global Competitiveness framework assessed a broader set of pillars including institutions, infrastructure, macroeconomic stability, health, education, market efficiency and innovation
'Doing Business' measured only innovation capacity of large corporations
Global Competitiveness Index measured only ease of paying taxes
advanced.e: 'Doing Business' focused narrowly on specific regulatory processes affecting business ease, while the Global Competitiveness framework used a much broader set of pillars (institutions, infrastructure, macro-stability, health, education, market efficiency, innovation, etc.) to assess overall economic competitiveness.
